title: ModGUI
description: GUI-based moderation tools for Paper servers. Punishment, investigation, and reporting with Discord webhook integration.
body:
# ModGUI
**ModGUI** is a staff moderation plugin for Paper servers that replaces chat commands with clean, click-through GUIs. Punish, investigate, and manage players, all without ever typing a command!

## Features
- **Punishment GUI:** Open a fully configurable punishment menu on any player. Each punishment type, icon, command, and available durations are defined in `config.yml`, so ModGUI works alongside any punishment plugin (LiteBans, AdvancedBan, EssentialsX, and more)!
  
- **Investigate GUI:** Right-click any player with the staff compass to instantly open their investigation panel. View anticheat flags for the current session with violation counts, ping, TPS, and timestamps. Includes GrimAC integration out of the box.
  
- **Player Reports:** Players can submit reports via `/report` with optional severity levels. A configurable cooldown prevents spam.
  
- **Staff Notes:** Add notes against a player directly from the investigate GUI, logged to Discord.
  
- **Discord Webhooks:** Punishments, anticheat alerts, reports, and staff notes all log to Discord with rich embeds. Role pings supported per event type.
  
- **Staff Compass:** A special compass item that opens the investigate GUI on right-click. Can't be dropped or lost on death.

## Commands

| Command | Description | Permission |
|---|---|---|
| `/punish <player>` | Opens the punishment GUI | Any `modgui.punish.*` node |
| `/investigate <player>` | Opens the investigate GUI | `modgui.investigate` |
| `/report <player> [severity] <reason>` | Submit a report against a player | `modgui.report` |
| `/modgui spyglass` | Gives you the staff compass | `modgui.spyglass` |
| `/modgui reload` | Reloads config and messages | `modgui.admin` |

## Permissions

| Permission | Description | Default |
|---|---|---|
| `modgui.admin` | Full access, includes all punish, investigate, notes, and spyglass permissions | OP |
| `modgui.punish.*` | All punishment types | false |
| `modgui.punish.warn` | Can warn players | false |
| `modgui.punish.kick` | Can kick players | false |
| `modgui.punish.mute` | Can mute players | false |
| `modgui.punish.tempban` | Can temporarily ban players | false |
| `modgui.punish.ban` | Can permanently ban players | false |
| `modgui.investigate` | Can open the investigate GUI | false |
| `modgui.notes.add` | Can add staff notes | false |
| `modgui.spyglass` | Can receive and use the staff compass | false |
| `modgui.report` | Can submit reports via `/report` | true |
| `modgui.exempt` | Cannot be punished, investigated, or reported through ModGUI | false |

## Configuration
All punishment types, durations, borders, messages, and webhook URLs are defined in `config.yml`. Full LuckPerms support with granular permission nodes per punishment type.

title: ProgressionRPGMob
description: Custom RPG mob spawner with configurable stats, names, and abilities — place named mobs at fixed locations that respawn automatically after death.
body:
# 👾 ProgressionRPGMob

ProgressionRPGMob lets you place named custom mobs at fixed world locations. Each mob has configurable health, damage, display name, and abilities. When killed, they respawn after a configurable delay — perfect for dungeon bosses, world guards, and repeatable farming spots.

No mob spawner blocks. No timers to manage. Place the mob, configure it once, and it just works.

## Features

- **Fixed-location spawning** — mobs are placed at exact coordinates
- **Configurable stats** — health, damage, speed, follow range per mob type
- **Custom display names** — full MiniMessage/color support
- **Auto-respawn** — configurable respawn delay after death
- **Mob editor** — edit placed mobs in-world without editing files
- **Save/load system** — all placements survive restarts
- **Admin tools** — give spawn tool, list, remove, reload

## Commands

| Command | Description |
|---|---|
| `/prpgm give` | Get the mob placement tool |
| `/prpgm save <name>` | Save current mob config as a template |
| `/prpgm edit <name>` | Edit a placed mob |
| `/prpgm list` | List all placed mobs |
| `/prpgm remove <name>` | Remove a placed mob |
| `/prpgm reload` | Reload config |

## Dependencies

Requires **ProgressionAPI**.

---

title: SuperPlayer
description: This project add ability commands to your server!
body:
# Superplayer Abilities Plugin

Superplayer is a lightweight, performance-focused administration and gameplay enhancement plugin for modern Paper/Spigot servers. It grants players access to four game-changing, visual-heavy tactical abilities, completely managed by a responsive cooldown and custom admin bypass system.

Built entirely upon modern execution methods, all visual elements interact on a client-side basis, ensuring your server remains lag-free while running beautifully.

## Key Features
⚡ Four Custom Player Abilities: A tailored set of tactical powers built to shift the tide of battle, tracking, or resource gathering.

## Available Abilities

### /ability radar
Instantly sweeps a 100-block field around you. If nearby players are detected, a persistent, vertical column of crimson tracker particles highlights their exact spatial layout through solid blocks, blocks, or terrain—visible only to you.

### /ability buff
Instantly channels combat enhancements to your character. Provides exactly 1 minute of high-tier status effects, including Regeneration II, Strength II, Speed II, Resistance II, and Saturation II.

### /ability pull
Harness gravitational pull to control the battlefield. Instantly pulls all living entities (monsters, animals, and enemy players) within a tight 30-block radius directly to your exact spatial coordinates using a clean velocity-vector arc.

### /ability xrayer
Scans a 30-block cube directly around your position for ultra-valuable assets (Diamonds, Emeralds, Gold, Iron, Lapis, and Ancient Debris). Discovered ores are instantly encased in a vivid, color-coded, glowing wireframe outline (Block Displays) piercing directly through the walls for 10 seconds.

title: Request Location
description: Request other people's location with a simple command
body:
## Why use this plugin?
This plugin allows for easier coordination between players. If for example chat was disabled, Request Location would allow players to still give their location to other people. Even if chat is enabled, the copy-to-clipboard feature makes it much simpler to put a player's location into your waypoint mod.

## How to use
Simply just use the requestlocation command with a username and you will then send a location request to that player. Within 60 seconds of your request, the player can choose to either accept or deny it (via buttons or commands). If they accept your request, you're given their location in a readable format, telling you either their distance from you or their dimension (if not in the same as you).

## Commands
- `requestlocation PLAYER_USERNAME` - Requests the location of a player
- `requestlocation accept` - Accepts your latest request
- `requestlocation deny` - Denies your latest request

## 🌟 Key Features

### 📅 Advanced Death History
- **Multi-Record Storage**: Saves the last **10 deaths** per player.
- **Detailed Metadata**: Each record tracks the exact **Date, Time, Coordinates (X, Y, Z)**, and the **Dimension** (Overworld, Nether, End).
- **Dynamic UI**: A beautiful "Death History" menu where each record is represented by a **Player Head** showing the actual skin of the player.

### 🛡️ Precise Restoration Logic
- **Perfect Slot Matching**: Items are restored to their exact original slots (Armor, Hotbar, Offhand, etc.).
- **Persistence**: Items remain visible in the death UI even after restoration, allowing for multiple retrievals if needed.
- **Re-Restore Safety**: A confirmation prompt prevents accidental repeated restorations: *"You have already restored these items, would you like to do it again?"*

### 👑 Flexible Permissions
- **Creative Mode**: Instant, one-click restoration.
- **Operators (OP)**: 
  - Access a confirmation UI for their own restorations.
  - **Inspection Mode**: Use `/invdeath <username>` to view another player's death history in a **strict view-only mode**.
- **Survival Players**: Blocked from unauthorized interactions with a clear permission message.

### 🌌 Ender Chest Support
- View-only access to saved Ender Chest contents from previous deaths.
- Renamed command `/invdeath-ender` for quick access.

---

## 💻 Commands

- /invdeath [username]: Open the Death History menu for yourself or another player (requires OP).
- `/invdeath-ender [username]`: Open the saved Ender Chest history (requires OP for others).

---

## 🛠️ Installation
1. Install **Fabric Loader** for Minecraft 1.21.1 - 1.21.11.
2. Download and place the mod jar in your `mods` folder.
3. Ensure **Fabric API** is also installed.

---

**Created by RO4449.**

title: Vincible Moon Datapack
description: Dependency for upcoming update 2.0 of The Vincible plugin, planned to be optional
body:
# Lunar Descent

A stylized moon dimension for Paper 1.21.1 servers. Fly high enough and leave the world behind.

---

## Traveling to the Moon

Reach **Y=500** in the overworld while flying and you'll breach the atmosphere. A brief blindness transition plays, then you're dropped onto the lunar surface. To return, do the same thing from the moon — fly to Y=500 and you'll re-enter the atmosphere and land back at the exact coordinates you left from.

---

## The Dimension

The moon uses the **End skybox** — pure black void with stars. No weather, no day cycle, fixed night, and low ambient lighting. The surface is made entirely from a handpicked palette of vanilla blocks:

- **Calcite** — primary surface, bright and sterile
- **Tuff** — scattered patches for variation
- **Smooth Basalt** — darker surface regions and deep bedrock layer
- **Basalt** — crater rims and maria patches
- **Dead Tube Coral Block** — dark spots across the surface
- **Cobbled Deepslate** — crater floors
- **Cyan Terracotta** — sub-surface layer
- **End Stone** — deep underground filler

---

## Terrain & Features

The terrain generates as gently rolling plains with no oceans or caves. On top of that, several features scatter across every chunk:

**Craters** — small (radius 2–5) and large (radius 6–12) impact craters with cobbled deepslate floors and basalt rims, generated fresh every chunk.

**Maria patches** — dark basalt and smooth basalt regions mimicking the moon's real dark seas.

**Dead coral spots** — small scattered dark patches across the surface.

---

## Ores

All ores spawn as their **deepslate variants** embedded in the sub-surface layers. Rarity and depth follow a realistic distribution:

| Ore | Depth | Rarity |
|-----|-------|--------|
| Coal | 20–55 | Common |
| Copper | 10–50 | Common |
| Iron | 5–50 | Common |
| Gold | 0–30 | Uncommon |
| Lapis | 0–35 | Uncommon |
| Redstone | 0–25 | Uncommon |
| Diamond | 0–15 | Rare |
| Emerald | 0–10 | Very rare |

---

## Lunar Pods

Scattered roughly every **1000 blocks** across the surface, lunar pods are small structures — a ring of smooth basalt and cobbled deepslate with a **barrel at the center**. Inside the barrel you'll find the **Viltrum Serum**, a one-of-a-kind item that permanently grants Viltrumite powers when consumed.

> Requires the [Vincible plugin](https://www.curseforge.com) to be installed for the serum effect to activate.

---

## Requirements

- Paper 1.21.1
- Java 21
- Vincible plugin (for the Viltrum Serum item effect)

title: One Player Tools
description: This datapack makes it so only one type of tool or armor can exist between all players.
body:
## **⚔️ One Person Tools (OPT)**
The ultimate "sharing is caring" nightmare.

Ever felt like Minecraft was too easy with everyone having their own gear? One Person Tools introduces a competitive twist where only one instance of a specific item can exist across the entire server.

This datapack is perfect for speedrunning to make it chaotic or regular survival to annoy your friends.

## **🕹️ How It Works**
If you craft a Diamond Pickaxe, you are the exclusive holder. The moment another player crafts or picks up a Diamond Pickaxe, yours instantly vanishes from your inventory, and they become the new holder.

Whether you’re speedrunning or just trying to survive, you’ll have to move fast or play dirty to keep your gear!

## **✨ Key Features**
- Works across all players. Only one person gets the tool at a time.

- Don't want to fight over the same item? Use the in-game menu to enable or disable specific items.

- Keep the chaos quiet or announce every theft with customizable chat notifications.

- Lightweight and designed to work with Minecraft 1.21.11.

## **⚙️ Quick Start**
Default Menu Key: Press G

From the menu, you can toggle item categories (Tools, Armor, Weapons) and manage notification settings.

## **🛠️ Installation Guide**
Download the OPT.zip file.

Navigate to your Minecraft world folder and drop the zip into the datapacks folder.

Important: Ensure you are at the Main Menu or have the world closed when applying the pack to ensure the Menu works correctly.

Launch the world and have fun!

## **📝 Compatibility**
Version: 1.21.11

_Multiplayer: Highly recommended! (Technically works in Singleplayer, but you'll just be fighting your own shadow)._

body:
### Introducing Ember Optimizations Ember Optimizations is a Forge modpack for Minecraft 1.20.1 built for one purpose — to make the game run the way it should. Whether you're on a budget laptop or a high-end rig, Ember delivers a smoother, more responsive experience without stripping away what makes Minecraft feel like Minecraft. ### From the Creators of Prism Optimized Ember Optimizations is made by me [(SodaPlays)](https://modrinth.com/user/SodaPlays). I am the person behind **Prism Optimized**. This modpack was built from the ground up for Forge. If you've used Prism before, you'll feel right at home. Same philosophy, same attention to detail, different loader.
![Ember Optimizations](https://cdn.modrinth.com/data/cached_images/a887b45126b775f5dd5beb154e07186ceb56c80e.png) [![Discord](https://i.imgur.com/j51LDaQ.png)](https://discord.gg/DMV28j3BSK) [![Bluesky](https://i.imgur.com/8WtUbWY.png)](https://bsky.app/profile/sodaplays.bsky.social) [![YouTube](https://i.imgur.com/USGe94v.png)](https://www.youtube.com/@SodaPlays_YT/videos)
### Performance & Stability At its core, Ember is built around a carefully selected set of optimization mods, all configured to work together rather than against each other. From chunk loading to entity rendering, every system has been tuned to reduce stutters, lower memory usage, and push frame rates as high as your hardware allows. ### OptiFine Feature Support Leaving OptiFine behind doesn't mean leaving your resource packs behind. Ember includes ETF (Entity Texture Features), EMF (Entity Model Features), and Continuity, covering the vast majority of OptiFine-dependent features, including custom entity textures, model overrides, and connected textures. For most packs, you can drop them straight in, and they'll just work. ### Shader Support Ember ships with Oculus, bringing full shader support to Forge. Whether you want to play vanilla or completely transform the look of the game with shaders, both are supported out of the box. ### What's Included
General Mods - Embeddium + FerriteCore + ModernFix for core performance gains - Entity Culling + ImmediatelyFast for rendering efficiency - Concurrent Chunk Management Engine for smooth chunk loading at any render distance - ETF, EMF, Continuity, and OptiGUI for OptiFine resource pack compatibility - Oculus for shader support - And more — all pre-configured and ready to go
### People Behind EO (Ember Optimizations) I want to say a special thanks to these people for helping with the creation of **EO** and **PO**! - [Vinyard](https://modrinth.com/user/Vinyard) - [Toasty_Toaster](https://modrinth.com/user/Toasty_Toaster) - [kibble_](https://modrinth.com/user/kibble_)

body:
I Lov Watr is my very first data pack, created with an important mission. It turns ordinary survival into an ecological challenge. Now your actions directly affect the state of the world's water. This is not just a game, it is a story about how easy it is to destroy a fragile ecosystem and how important it is to protect it.



Water Points (WP) System

The main feature of the datapack is the dynamic Water Points system. It is an indicator of the health of the aquatic world:



Pollution is punished: if you kill fish and harm the aquatic ecosystem in any way, your WP will drop. A low score will lead to catastrophic consequences: from poisoning to blindness in the water.

Care is rewarded: restore the ecosystem and keep order. A high WP level will give you dolphin grace and make the world around you truly alive.

title: Camera For Streaming
description: Camera that automatically follows players in game.
body:
# **UNIQUE DEVELOPMENT**

Have you ever wanted to stream what's happening on your server? Randomly watch what players are doing from different angles and switch between players?

Luckily for you, there's my **INCREDIBLE** plugin that makes it possible!

I originally made this for my Paper server on version 1.21.1, but I think it should work on higher versions too.

_Plugin inspired by the Makoto server_

So, the plugin includes:

## **EASY CONFIGURATION**

The config allows you to:
- Instantly add a player who will automatically switch to camera mode upon joining to observe the server (works 50/50)
- Change the interval between switching camera angles and players!
- Also change the camera's position when no players are online

Even if no one is on the server, the camera will teleport to your specified coordinates and slowly rotate 360 degrees in a circle!

### **NOTICE**
The plugin does NOT help you stream — it doesn't include any streaming functionality. It allows you to turn a player into a camera so you can stream from their perspective using OBS or similar software.

### COMMANDS

- `/resetcamera <nickname>` — removes a player from the camera role  
- `/spectatorcameramod <nickname>` — sets a player as the camera  
- `/cameraspectate <nickname>/random` — if you enter a **player's nickname**, you’ll view only that player in camera mode without switching. If you write **random** instead, the camera will randomly teleport to different players and watch them

If you run into any issues, contact me on Telegram! @AlexsandrDeveloper  
_(Also message me if you're interested in buying the plugin’s source code)_

# PacketLimiter
**Protect your server from packet spam and network abuse.**

PacketLimiter monitors player network traffic in real-time and automatically warns or kicks players who exceed configurable packet limits. Perfect for preventing lag machines, book bans, chunk bans, auto-clickers, and packet-based crash exploits.

## Features

- Configurable packet limits - Set max packets per second and per tick
- Warning system - Warn players before kicking, with persistent warnings across rejoins
- Join grace period - New players get a configurable grace period before limits apply
- Lightweight - Minimal performance impact, runs efficiently in the background
- Fully configurable - Edit all limits in config.yml





## Config

```
# PacketLimiter Configuration

# Maximum packets allowed per second
max-packets-per-second: 40

# Maximum packets allowed in a single tick
max-packets-per-tick: 5

# Number of warnings before kick
max-warnings: 3

# Grace period in milliseconds after joining (10 seconds)
grace-period-ms: 10000
```

title: Deadman's Chest
description: Find drifting barrels, reveal soggy pirate maps, follow them to cursed markers, defeat skeletal guardians, and claim buried treasure.
body:
Deadman's Chest

Drifting barrels, soggy pirate maps, cursed guardians, and buried treasure for PaperMC servers.

No resource pack. No NMS. Just pirate treasure hunts built with supported Paper/Bukkit APIs.

--- ## What Is Deadman's Chest? **Deadman's Chest** turns the open ocean into the beginning of a survival-friendly pirate adventure. While exploring the world, players may discover strange glowing barrels drifting in the water. Claim the soggy map inside, follow the skull-marked chart, locate the cursed treasure marker, defeat the guardians, and claim whatever the dead left behind. But treasure is never truly free. A dead pirate does not give up his loot willingly. --- ## The Gameplay Loop Deadman's Chest is built around a complete treasure-hunt loop: ```text Find a drifting barrel -> Claim the soggy treasure map -> Watch the wet parchment reveal itself -> Follow the skull-marked chart -> Discover the cursed treasure marker -> Activate the marker -> Defeat the skeleton guardians -> Watch as the chest is revealed -> Loot the treasure -> See the chest cleansed and vanish ``` The goal is not to create a complicated quest system. The goal is to add mystery, danger, and reward to normal survival exploration. --- ## Features * Floating treasure barrels that spawn in the world using custom models * Three treasure tiers: **Emerald**, **Ruby**, and **Diamond** * Custom soggy parchment-style treasure maps * Animated wet-map reveal effect * Skull-and-crossbones treasure marker drawn directly onto the map * Standard Minecraft player tracking cursor on the custom map * Cursed treasure markers placed in the world * Skeleton guardian encounters based on treasure tier * Custom treasure chest model * Chest reveal animation after guardians are defeated * Chest loot inventory instead of forced item delivery * Chest remains while loot is still present * Chest vanishes with a cleansing effect once emptied * Configurable loot tables * Support for enchanted book rewards * Support for custom configured loot * Operator cleanup command for Deadman's Chest entities * No resource pack required * No NMS or internal server classes Deadman's Chest is designed to feel like something that belongs naturally in a survival world: rare, atmospheric, dangerous, and rewarding. --- ## Treasure Tiers Deadman's Chest uses three visual treasure tiers. Each tier carries through the entire hunt: ```text barrel band -> map skull color -> treasure marker gem -> treasure chest gem ``` | Tier | Theme | Description | | ----------- | ------------ | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | | **Emerald** | Green | The most common treasure tier. A good early-to-mid survival reward. | | **Ruby** | Redstone red | A stronger treasure tier with better rewards and tougher guardians. | | **Diamond** | Diamond blue | The highest treasure tier, guarded by the strongest encounter and capable of rare rewards. | The tier is visible before the fight begins, giving players a chance to decide how prepared they want to be. Bring a sword. Bring a shield. Bring friends. Bring wolves. Maybe bring iron blocks and pumpkins if you like solving problems the Minecraft way. --- ## Screenshots and Videos ### Finding a Barrel ![Finding a Barrel](https://cdn.modrinth.com/data/cached_images/9716da1d7e2fe51858bcfd3ef5388039198357cf.jpeg) ### Receiving a Soggy Map ![Recieving the Soggy Map](https://cdn.modrinth.com/data/cached_images/15255da29c384d373c1dfc3250d4365d51f37e8b.jpeg) ### Following the Treasure Map ![Following the Map](https://cdn.modrinth.com/data/cached_images/f5265ceb59f1a6ace6bac312c832dcc38d4837c2.jpeg) ### Discovering the Treasure Marker ![Discovering the Treasurer Marker](https://cdn.modrinth.com/data/cached_images/8b457d5e67e9d934123de4aa11aaef250a1aaee7.jpeg) ### Fighting the Guardians ![Fighting the Guardians](https://cdn.modrinth.com/data/cached_images/0e45ccd403ba7f320a961fa60a5d77195b5e1cac.jpeg) ### Guardians Defeated ![Guardians Defeated](https://cdn.modrinth.com/data/cached_images/77e3d1814b50f2bfb899ca67e5ca6d0586b214a3.jpeg) ### Chest Rises ![Chest Rises](https://cdn.modrinth.com/data/cached_images/841caf58aa3d5a601dac5f760218e20b7918342a.jpeg) Videos:

Watching the soggy map reveal

Reaching the marker and triggering the guardians

The chest is revealed

Getting the loot and cleansing the location

--- ## Why This Exists Minecraft survival already has wonderful systems: * oceans * maps * exploration * hostile mobs * wolves * iron golems * enchanted gear * rare resources * strange places in the world Deadman's Chest tries to connect those systems into a small adventure. It gives players a reason to sail, explore, prepare, fight, and return home with a story. It also provides an alternate path to meaningful rewards such as enchanted books and useful supplies, especially for servers that do not want villager trading halls to dominate progression. --- ## Installation 1. Download the latest release. 2. Drop the plugin jar into your server's `plugins/` directory. 3. Start or restart the server. 4. Review the generated configuration file. 5. Watch the waters. When the plugin is running, treasure barrels may begin appearing in valid water locations depending on your configuration. --- ## Requirements * **PaperMC** * **Java 21+** * Minecraft/Paper version targeted by the current release ### Tested Against * Paper 1.21.x/Java 21 * Paper 26.+/Java 25 Deadman's Chest uses supported Bukkit/Paper APIs and does not rely on NMS or internal server classes. --- ## Configuration Deadman's Chest is intended to be configurable while still having sensible defaults. Configuration areas include: * Barrel spawn limits * Barrel lifetime * Treasure generation distance * Treasure tier weighting * Loot tables * Enchanted book chances * Custom loot additions * Cleanup/debug behavior Example configuration shape: ```yaml debug: true messages: treasure-recovered: enabled: true broadcast: false text: "%player% has recovered the treasure of %adjective% pirate %pirate_name% and broken the curse." barrels: max-active: 30 min-lifetime-minutes: 4 max-lifetime-minutes: 12 seconds-between-spawn-checks: 30 min-distance-between-barrels: 128 loot: remove-defaults: false level-1: rolls: 4 remove: - minecraft:cooked_cod add: - material: minecraft:copper_ingot min: 4 max: 12 weight: 12 level-2: rolls: 6 book-chance-percent: 18 remove: [] add: - material: minecraft:lapis_lazuli min: 4 max: 16 weight: 8 add-books: - enchantment: minecraft:mending level: 1 weight: 1 - enchantment: minecraft:fortune level: 2 weight: 2 - enchantment: minecraft:efficiency level: 4 weight: 2 custom: - material: minecraft:iron_sword name: "Cursed Raider's Cutlass" min: 1 max: 1 weight: 2 enchants: - enchantment: minecraft:sharpness level: 3 - enchantment: minecraft:vanishing_curse level: 1 - material: minecraft:iron_chestplate name: "Salt-Stained Breastplate" min: 1 max: 1 weight: 2 enchants: - enchantment: minecraft:protection level: 3 - enchantment: minecraft:binding_curse level: 1 level-3: rolls: 8 book-chance-percent: 35 remove: - minecraft:enchanted_golden_apple add: - material: minecraft:diamond min: 2 max: 5 weight: 8 - material: minecraft:trident min: 1 max: 1 weight: 1 add-books: - enchantment: minecraft:mending level: 1 weight: 2 - enchantment: minecraft:fortune level: 3 weight: 3 - enchantment: minecraft:efficiency level: 5 weight: 4 - enchantment: minecraft:protection level: 4 weight: 4 - enchantment: minecraft:sharpness level: 5 weight: 4 custom: - material: minecraft:diamond_sword name: "Deadman's Blade" min: 1 max: 1 weight: 1 enchants: - enchantment: minecraft:sharpness level: 5 - enchantment: minecraft:fire_aspect level: 2 - material: minecraft:diamond_pickaxe name: "Buried King's Pick" min: 1 max: 1 weight: 1 enchants: - enchantment: minecraft:efficiency level: 5 - enchantment: minecraft:fortune level: 3 ``` Exact configuration options may change during beta as gameplay balance is tuned. --- ## Loot Treasure chests use a chest-sized inventory window. Loot is not forced directly into the player inventory. This avoids losing rewards when a player's inventory is full. Current behavior: ```text Player opens treasure chest -> Loot inventory appears -> Player takes items -> Chest remains if loot is still present -> Chest is removed only after the loot inventory is emptied ``` This makes the reward feel like an actual treasure chest rather than a simple item payout. ### Loot Categories Deadman's Chest loot may include: * Food * Ingots and gems * Experience bottles * Saplings and useful survival items * Armor * Tools * Weapons * Rare items * Enchanted books * Custom configured treasure items ### Enchanted Books Enchanted books can appear in higher-tier treasure. The intent is to make treasure hunting a meaningful alternate reward path without making books too common. Recommended balance: | Tier | Book Behavior | | ------- | --------------------------- | | Emerald | No premium books by default | | Ruby | Chance for useful books | | Diamond | Chance for top-tier books | A chest should never be flooded with books. Books are meant to feel special. ### Custom Loot Server owners may configure custom loot entries such as enchanted tools, armor, or weapons. Example: ```yaml loot: level-3: custom: - material: DIAMOND_SWORD name: "Deadman's Blade" min: 1 max: 1 weight: 1 enchants: - enchantment: sharpness level: 5 - enchantment: vanishing_curse level: 1 ``` Custom loot is intended for server owners who want to add their own flavor while preserving the core treasure-hunt experience. --- ## Encounters Treasure markers are not harmless decorations. When activated, they summon skeleton guardians. The number and strength of guardians depends on treasure level. | Tier | Encounter Feel | | ------- | -------------------------------------------- | | Emerald | Small fight | | Ruby | Moderate fight | | Diamond | Stronger fight with a captain-style guardian | Guardians are configured to avoid becoming gear farms. Their purpose is to protect the treasure, not to replace the reward chest. The encounter is designed to be dangerous but not absurd. Players can prepare using normal survival tools: * Better armor * Shields * Bows * Potions * Wolves * Friends * Iron golems * Terrain preparation Deadman's Chest creates the problem. Minecraft gives players many ways to solve it. --- ## World Atmosphere Deadman's Chest leans into a cursed pirate mood: * glowing barrels drifting at sea * damp parchment maps * skull-marked treasure locations * soul fire * skeleton guardians * treasure chests rising from the earth * lightning and fire cleansing the empty chest The plugin works in normal survival worlds, but it especially shines in atmospheric coastal, island, pirate, or night-focused servers. --- ## Commands Commands are primarily intended for operators and server recovery. | Command | Description | | ---------------------- | ------------------------------------------------- | | `/deadmanschest:info` | Shows current spawned barrel information. | | `/deadmanschest:flush` | Removes Deadman's Chest tagged world components. | Command behavior may change as the plugin matures. During beta, commands may be more permissive or debug-oriented than they will be in a final release. --- ## Operator Notes Deadman's Chest uses Display Entities, Interaction entities, PersistentDataContainer tags, and custom map renderers. Important behavior: * Barrels are transient and non-persistent. * Barrel counts are limited by configuration. * Treasure maps are player-held custom maps. * Treasure markers may persist in the world until activated. * Treasure chests remain only while loot remains. * Operator cleanup tools exist for removing Deadman's Chest world entities if needed. This design allows abandoned treasure markers to become atmospheric world dressing while still giving server operators a recovery path. --- ## Performance Notes Deadman's Chest is designed to keep active entity counts bounded. * Floating barrels are capped and time out. * Treasure markers are lightweight Display/Interaction compositions. * Guardians exist only during active encounters. * Treasure chests exist only while unclaimed or partially looted. * Cleanup commands are available for operators. The plugin avoids NMS and avoids resource-pack dependency. As with any plugin using visual entities, server owners should avoid extreme configuration values that create excessive numbers of active world objects. --- ## Current Status Deadman's Chest is released and functional on the listed tested versions of Minecraft. The full gameplay loop is playable: ```text barrel -> map -> marker -> guardians -> chest -> loot -> cleanup ``` Current focus areas: * Survival-world testing * Loot balance * Configuration polish * Edge-case cleanup * Documentation * Release packaging Feedback, bug reports, and suggestions are welcome. --- ## Design Philosophy Deadman's Chest is not meant to be a full quest engine. It is meant to add a small, memorable adventure to survival play. The best moments should feel like stories players tell afterward: * I saw something glowing out on the water. * The map was soaked, but it started to reveal itself. * We found the skull marker at night. * The skeletons came out of nowhere. * The chest rose out of the ground after the last guardian fell. * We got a Mending book and barely made it home. That is the experience this plugin is trying to create. --- ## Compatibility Deadman's Chest should work well with ordinary Paper survival servers. It is especially fun alongside plugins or server styles that encourage: * sailing * exploration * coastal bases * survival progression * dangerous nights * reduced villager-trading dependence * world ambience No client mod is required. No resource pack is required. --- ## Inspiration Deadman's Chest is inspired by: * pirate legends * cursed treasure * shipwreck stories * old parchment maps * strange things floating in the ocean * skeleton crews * survival worlds that reward exploration A pirate, even a dead one, is not going to give up his loot willingly. --- ## Other Projects Other projects of mine that you might enjoy [Simple Ships - build ships to sail the vast oceans](https://modrinth.com/plugin/simpleshipsplugin) --- ## License Deadman's Chest is licensed under the MIT License. See the [LICENSE](LICENSE) file for full details. --- ## Final Thoughts Deadman's Chest is meant to add mystery to the ocean and danger to treasure hunting. Not every barrel should be ignored. Not every map should be trusted. Not every treasure should be easy to claim.

description: A QoL auto-replant feature inspired by Hypixel's Replenish enchantment, but without the enchantment restrictions. Toggle it on/off anytime and it works globally across all tools and crops.
body:
# Replenish++ 🌾

Tiny, blazing-fast auto-replant QoL plugin for Spigot/Paper, inspired by Hypixel's Replenish mechanic.


![Preview](https://cdn.modrinth.com/data/9rWJrVZX/images/eab04933c367a681bc6f22210c05ae2e6d479c23.webp)

---

## What it does

- 🌾 Auto-replants Wheat, Carrots, Potatoes, Nether Wart, Cocoa, Beetroots, Torchflowers, and Pitcher Crops
- 🌱 Immature crops keep their current growth stage
- 🎒 Optional seed consumption (on by default)
- 📦 Optional direct pickup into your inventory (on by default)
- 🪓 Requires the correct tool (Hoes / Axes)
- 🧭 Correctly replants Cocoa with the proper facing
- 🍀 Fortune enchantments works normally
- ⚡ Designed for high-performance and large farms
- 🔊 Fully configurable sounds

---

## Quick install

1. Drop the JAR into `plugins/`
2. Start the server
3. Edit `plugins/Replenish/config.yml` if desired
4. Done.

---

## Default behavior (no config edits)

* Breaking a **mature** crop:

    * Replants at age **0**
    * Consumes **1 seed** from your inventory (or off-hand) if `requirePlayerSeed` is `true`
    * Drops go straight to you if `directPickup` is `true`

* Breaking an **immature** crop:
    * Replants at the **same age** (no seed needed)

---

## Commands & permissions

| Command              | Description               |
|----------------------|---------------------------|
| `/replenish status`  | Show current settings     |
| `/replenish version` | Show plugin version       |
| `/replenish toggle`  | Enable/disable the plugin |
| `/replenish reload`  | Reload the configuration  |

Permissions:

* `replenish.status` (default: **true**)
* `replenish.version` (default: **true**)
* `replenish.use` (default: **op**)
* `replenish.toggle` (default: **op**)
* `replenish.reload` (default: **op**)
* `replenish.*` (default: **op**)

---

## Configuration

### Common settings

```yaml
enabled: true
requirePlayerSeed: true
directPickup: true
replantDelayTicks: 1
maxReplantsPerTick: 1024
checkUpdates: true
```

<details>
<summary>Full default config.yml</summary>

```yaml
# ============================================
#         REPLENISH CONFIG
# ============================================

# --------------------------
# GENERAL SETTINGS
# --------------------------

config-version: 5              # DON'T TOUCH THIS!!!

enabled: true                  # master switch: false disables all replanting globally
requirePlayerSeed: true        # consume 1 seed from inventory on mature harvest
directPickup: true             # drops go straight to the player
replantDelayTicks: 1           # 1 tick = 50ms

maxReplantsPerTick: 1024      # maximum crops replanted per tick (20 ticks/second)
        # raise this on beefier servers if replants lag behind
# lower it on weaker servers to reduce load

checkUpdates: true             # check GitHub for new releases on server startup

# --------------------------
# CROP TOGGLES (turn on/off)
# --------------------------

crops:
  wheat: true
  carrots: true
  potatoes: true
  nether_wart: true
  cocoa: true
  beetroots: true

# --------------------------
# CHAT MESSAGES (customize these)
# --------------------------
# Placeholders: {crop}, {tool}, {seed}, {count}

messages:
  inventory-full: "&8[&eReplenish&8] &8» &7Your inventory was full, so some items dropped on the ground instead."
  requires-tool: "&8[&eReplenish&8] &8» &7You need a &e{tool} &7to harvest &e{crop}&7."
  need-seed: "&8[&eReplenish&8] &8» &7You need &e{count}x {seed} &7in your inventory to replant this."

# --------------------------
# SOUND EFFECTS (customize or disable)
# --------------------------
# Each of the four feedback sounds can be individually enabled/disabled
# and customized with any Bukkit Sound, volume, and pitch.
#
# sound:  Must match a Bukkit Sound enum name (case-insensitive).
#         Full list: https://hub.spigotmc.org/javadocs/spigot/org/bukkit/Sound.html
#         Invalid names log a warning and fall back to the default.
# volume: 0.0 (silent) to 1.0 (loudest)
# pitch:  0.5 (low) to 2.0 (high); 1.0 = normal
#
# To disable a sound entirely, set enabled: false.

sounds:
  # Played when harvested crops go into your inventory
  pickup:
    enabled: true
    sound: ENTITY_ITEM_PICKUP
    volume: 1.0
    pitch: 1.0

  # Played when your inventory is full and items drop on the ground
  inventory-full:
    enabled: true
    sound: BLOCK_NOTE_BLOCK_BASS
    volume: 1.0
    pitch: 0.5

  # Played when you try to harvest without the required tool
  denied-tool:
    enabled: true
    sound: ENTITY_VILLAGER_NO
    volume: 1.0
    pitch: 0.5

  # Played when you try to harvest but lack a seed to replant
  denied-seed:
    enabled: true
    sound: ENTITY_VILLAGER_NO
    volume: 1.0
    pitch: 0.5
```

</details>

## 💡 Contributions & Pull Requests

Managing direct PRs gets a bit overwhelming for me, so I keep them disabled for this project to protect my peace. But I'm open to discussion! If you have a features, optimizations, bug fixes, improvements etc., open an issue first. We can chat about it there and see if it fits the project.
Otherwise, you are highly encouraged to fork or clone this repo and do whatever you want with it. Vibe-code, rip it apart, and build what you want not what other people expect you to build.
Everyone starts somewhere, and you are goated. You matter, so go start now.

title: WEScreens
description: Meet WEScreens — a mod that lets you build functional menus right inside the game, without knowing how to code.
body:
# WEScreens

Create fully customizable in-game GUI screens for Minecraft Forge - without writing Java code.

**WEScreens** is a visual GUI editor that lets you design interfaces directly inside Minecraft. Create menus, dialogs, shops, quest windows, server information screens, and much more using an intuitive drag-and-drop editor. Save your screens to the world and open them instantly with commands.

## ⚠️ Beta Status

WEScreens is currently in **Beta stage**.

This means the mod is still under active development and may contain bugs, unfinished features, or unexpected behavior.

Please keep in mind:

* Some features may change or be reworked in future updates
* Bugs or crashes may occur in certain cases
* World data compatibility may not be guaranteed between versions
* Performance and stability improvements are ongoing

Feedback and bug reports are appreciated and help improve the mod.


## ✨ Features

* 🎨 Visual in-game GUI editor
* 🖱️ Drag & drop interface editing
* 📏 Move and resize elements freely
* 🔒 Lock elements to prevent accidental movement
* 📑 Multi-tab interfaces
* 📂 Nested containers with independent tabs
* 📝 Rich text with colors, alignment, and custom scaling
* 🖼️ Display any Minecraft texture
* ⚡ Execute commands with buttons
* 📦 Screens are automatically saved in world data
* 👥 Open screens for specific players using commands
* 🔄 Edit existing screens at any time

## 🧩 Available Components

* Text
* Images
* Close Buttons
* Command Buttons
* Tab Buttons
* Tab Containers
* Containers

## 🛠️ Commands

WEScreens provides two simple commands for creating and managing your custom interfaces.

* `/createscreen <name>`
  Creates a new screen and opens it in the visual editor.

* `/screen <name> <action> [new_name]`
  Manage an existing screen.

  **Available actions:**

  * `open` — Open the screen.
  * `edit` — Open the screen in the editor.
  * `rename` — Rename the screen (requires `new_name`).
  * `delete` — Delete the screen permanently.

**Example:**

```text
/screen MainMenu rename LobbyMenu
```


## 🔥 Dynamic Placeholders

Display real-time information inside your interfaces.

Examples:

* `%playername%`
* `%displayname%`
* `%health%`
* `%food%`
* `%xp%`
* `%level%`
* `%coords%`
* `%biome%`
* `%dimension%`
* `%time%`
* `%totalplayers%`

...and many more.

## 📚 Perfect For

* Rules screens
* Quest systems
* Tutorials
* Shops
* Admin panels
* Command hubs
* Factions & clans

## 🚀 Why WEScreens?

Unlike traditional GUI mods, WEScreens doesn't require creating a new GUI in code every time you need a menu.

Design, edit, and update interfaces directly in-game with a powerful visual editor, making iteration fast and simple while supporting everything from basic menus to complex multi-tab layouts.

Whether you're creating a modpack or adventure map, WEScreens provides a flexible and efficient way to build beautiful Minecraft interfaces.

title: Schworlium
description: Worley noise-based caves for Fabric and Neoforge
body:
Schworlium is a Worley-noise cave generation mod for Minecraft 26.2.x and 1.21.11 targeting both Fabric and NeoForge. Right now, It's essentially an opinionated port of SuperFluke's Worley's Caves, but it will eventually diverge into a more fleshed-out spelunking mod.

As expected, the carver replaces vanilla's caves with hollow networks shaped by 3D Worley noise.
  
The two substantive changes that pulled the project away from being a 1:1 port are a smoother carve and a taller working range. The original implementation contained jittery per-block math in its noise sampling and threshold logic that produced visibly clunky walls and unnatural seams between regions. This has been replaced with the smoothing approach used in Worlium, yielding cleaner surfaces and more coherent cave shapes. Separately, the carver has been adapted to the post-1.18 extended world height. Due to this change, certain configuration options that no longer made sense were dropped at the same time.

Compatible worldgen mods:

- Tectonic
- Terralith
- Moderner Beta
- Geophilic
- Subsurface

title: COAL — Cloth Config adapter
description: Renders every COAL-using mod's settings screen in Cloth Config.
body:
Renders every [COAL](https://modrinth.com/mod/config-object-abstraction-lib)-using mod's settings screen
in [Cloth Config](https://modrinth.com/mod/cloth-config), plus JSON
persistence, load-time validation, and versioned migrations.

## For players

Install **all three** side-by-side in your `mods/` folder:

1. **[COAL](https://modrinth.com/mod/config-object-abstraction-lib)** — the abstraction layer that COAL-consuming mods depend on.
2. **coal-cloth-adapter** — this mod.
3. **[Cloth Config](https://modrinth.com/mod/cloth-config)** — the GUI library that actually renders the screens.

Any mod that consumes COAL will use Cloth Config for its settings screen once
these three are installed together.

### Cloth vs. YACL

Cloth Config's sub-category widget recurses cleanly, so this adapter
preserves deep-nested config trees end-to-end. YACL's equivalent flattens
after two levels. If your mods declare heavily-nested configs and you want
every level preserved in the GUI, pick this adapter.

### Don't install alongside `coal-yacl-adapter`

Only **one** COAL adapter should be installed at a time. If you'd rather use
YACL, install [`coal-yacl-adapter`](https://modrinth.com/mod/coal-yacl-adapter)
instead of this one.

## For mod authors

You don't compile against this mod. Depend on `coal-api` +
`coal-api-gui-<loader>` at compile time; your users install whichever adapter
they prefer at runtime. See the [docs](https://mc.oliveryasuna.com/coal/) for
the walkthrough.

## Feature coverage

Advertises `MIGRATION`, `VALIDATION`, and `GUI_DELEGATION`. Does not advertise
`SYNC`, `FILE_WATCH`, `JSON5`, or `CUSTOM_FORMATS` — see the module README on
GitHub for the full annotation-to-widget mapping and known limitations.

## Links

- [Documentation](https://mc.oliveryasuna.com/)
- [Source code](https://github.com/oliveryasuna/minecraft-mods)
- [Sibling: `coal-yacl-adapter`](https://modrinth.com/mod/coal-yacl-adapter)

title: Teleport Player
description: This project add a way to tp other players for the no-op
body:
# TPA Datapack

A simple and lightweight Teleport Request (TPA) system for Minecraft, powered by datapacks and scoreboards.

## Features

- Request to teleport to another player using `/trigger`
- Target player receives a clickable message to accept the request
- Once accepted, the requester is instantly teleported to the target's location
- No commands registration required — uses vanilla `/trigger` mechanics

## Requirements

- **Minecraft Java Edition**
- **Scoreboard ID Mod (Required Dependency)**  
  This datapack relies on the **scoreboard id** feature provided by a mod or data-driven system that assigns unique IDs via scoreboard objectives.  
  **Must be installed and enabled before loading this datapack.**

## How to Use

1. **Send a TPA Request**  
   Run the following command in chat:
   ```/trigger teleport.tpa set <player_id>```
Replace `<player_id>` with the target player's **scoreboard ID**.

2. **Receive the Request**  
The target player will receive a chat message with a clickable `[Accept]` button.

3. **Accept the Request**  
The target player clicks `[Accept]`.  
→ The requester is immediately teleported to their location.

## Notes

- Only one active request per player at a time.
- Requests automatically expire after a short duration if not accepted.
- This datapack does not modify core gameplay mechanics beyond teleportation.
- Compatible with multiplayer servers.

## Installation

1. Download and place the datapack into your world's `datapacks` folder.
2. Restart the server or run `/reload`.
3. Ensure the **Scoreboard ID** dependency is properly configured.

## Uninstallation

1. Delete the datapack from the `datapacks` folder.
2. Run `/reload`.
3. Optionally remove related scoreboard objectives if no longer needed.

---

*Simple. Fast. Vanilla-friendly.*

title: IBCarpet
description: A carpet extension mod and a port of JoaCarpet's insane behavior feature to the newer version of Minecraft. This is used to manipulate item entity RNG.
body:
# ibcarpet

A carpet extension mod. A port of
[JoaCarpet](https://github.com/JoakimThorsen/JoaCarpet)'s insane behavior
feature to the newer version of Minecraft.

Insane behavior is used to test item entity RNG by giving user control over the
random number generator to forcibly generate highly unlikely numbers without
waiting for hours.

Currently, this extension supports item entity RNG controls over the following actions:

- Breaking minecart
- Piston breaking blocks
- Breaking containers (chest, dropper, hopper)
- Dispense RNG (dispenser, crafter, dropper)
- Projectile

## Usage

To start using IBCarpet (Insane Behaviors Carpet): `/carpet insaneBehaviors
true`. Put false instead of true if you want to turn everything off.

By default, ibcarpet uses the trimodal distribution with an extremeness value of
0.5. The distributions provided by this mod can be configured using `/carpet
ibDistribution <distributionName>`. Distributions controls how random numbers
are picked. Read the distribution description below to understand when to use
what.

## Distributions

- Minecraft default: [Triangle](#triangle-distribution)
- [Uniform](#uniform-distribution)
- [Bimodal](#bimodal-distribution)
- IBCarpet default: [Trimodal](#trimodal-distribution)
- [Discrete](#discrete-distribution)

### Triangle Distribution

This is the random number generator used by most of Minecraft's default item
entity position and velocity RNG. IBCarpet replaces these triangle distribution
random numbers with custom ones where the users can freely modify to fit their
needs. Some of the RNG replaced by IBCarpet are from a uniform distribution
instead of triangle distribution, but it does not affect the overall purpose of
IBCarpet at all.

Here's the current implementation of Minecraft's triangle distribution RNG:

```java
default double triangle(final double mean, final double spread) {
  return mean + spread * (this.nextDouble() - this.nextDouble());
}
```

`this.nextDouble()` generates a number within `[0, 1)` uniformly. `mean` and
`spread` are constants most of the time, and they are not something we need to
worry about for understanding how to use IBCarpet.

`this.nextDouble() - this.nextDouble()` is what gives the shape of the triangle
distribution. If we run this a bunch of times and collect the outputs into a
histogram where the Y-axis is the probability of numbers within that range on
the X-axis getting picked, it will look like this:

![Triangle Distribution](https://github.com/TKperson/ibcarpet/blob/main/assets/triangle_distribution.png?raw=true)

The shape looks like a triangle where the peak is at 0, and the frequency
decreases as the RNG generates numbers closer to -1 and 1. This is exactly the
behavior we see in vanilla Minecraft. For example, a dropper dispenses items into
random directions, but from time to time, there will be one or a few items that
travels further than the rest. This is due to Minecraft's RNG picking
numbers from a triangle distribution; it mimics a normal distribution (bell
curve) where values further from the center are highly unlikely to happen, but
will happen eventually given enough time.

This is the reason why insane behaviors is useful to a lot of technical
players. Instead of testing/waiting for a really long time to catch highly
unlikely events, this carpet extension allows players to catch those events
much faster.

### Uniform Distribution

![Uniform Distribution](https://github.com/TKperson/ibcarpet/blob/main/assets/uniform_distribution.png?raw=true)

All numbers are equally likely to be picked inside of this distribution. This
is useful when testing a design for a long period of time. Uniform distribution
will most likely catch all edge cases when given enough time.

### Bimodal Distribution

![Bimodal Distribution](https://github.com/TKperson/ibcarpet/blob/main/assets/bimodal_distribution.png?raw=true)

This distribution is the complete opposite of triangle distribution, where all
the unlikely events from the triangle distribution are likely to happen in
the bimodal distribution. This is useful to test only the very rare edge cases.

The extremeness of this distribution can be configured using `/carpet
ibBimodalExtremeness <value>`. `value` can be a number between `0` and `1`, but
can't be exactly `1`. `0` means uniform distribution and values closer to `1`
means "very extreme edges." The default extremeness value is `0.5`.

### Trimodal Distribution

![Trimodal Distribution](https://github.com/TKperson/ibcarpet/blob/main/assets/trimodal_distribution.png?raw=true)

This distribution is similar to bimodal, but values around -1, 0, and 1 are
more likely to happen instead of just values around -1 and 1. Bimodal
distribution is not great at covering axis-aligned extremes. For example, when
an item is dispensed from a dropper, it will pick a random velocity vector in
the X and Z axes. Bimodal can only increase the probability of both X and Z to
an extreme, it cannot increase only one axis at a time. This means, in this
case, if bimodal has a high extreme value, it's only useful for testing items
being dispensed diagonally, which can miss some edge cases that happen when
items travel parallel to the world axes.

The extremeness of this distribution can be configured using `/carpet
ibTrimodalExtremeness <value>`. `value` can be a number between 0 and 1, but
can't be 1. `0` means uniform distribution and values closer to `1` means "very
extreme edges and center." The default extremeness value is `0.5`. Note that
this value does not change the distribution as much as the bimodal extremeness
value to its distribution.

### Discrete Distribution

![Discrete Distribution](https://github.com/TKperson/ibcarpet/blob/main/assets/discrete_distribution.png?raw=true)

Unlike the other distributions, discrete distribution is not continuous. It
picks number randomly based on a pre-determined set of possible numbers. This
set of numbers can be configured using `/carpet ibDiscreteCuts <value>`. It's
better to show the pattern than explaining how discrete random numbers are
generated in IBCarpet.

Here's the pattern:

- Cut = 0, possible numbers are `[0, 1]`
- Cut = 1, possible numbers are `[0, 0.5, 1]`
- Cut = 2, possible numbers are `[0, 0.333..., 0.666..., 1]`
- Cut = 3, possible numbers are `[0, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 1]`

The possible numbers are like evenly slicing up a cake. The space between each
cut becomes thinner as the number of cuts increases. A value is picked from
this set of possible numbers as the generated number. As the number of cuts
approaches infinity, the distribution becomes uniform.

Discrete distribution is useful to test most of the possible edge cases very
quickly. Since it has a limited amount of possible numbers, it's very easy to
generate extreme values. Please do remember that discrete distribution can help
players to quickly generate many important and unique extreme values, but it
does not cover all possibilities.

Unlike other distributions, this one has a range of `[-1, 1]` (inclusive)
instead of `(-1, 1)` (exclusive).

The default number of cuts is `4`. Discrete distribution supersedes the
systematic method of generating random numbers used in the original JoaCarpet
extension.

## Differences between JoaCarpet

JoaCarpet generates random number similar to the discrete distribution. However,
two main differences are that discrete distribution is independent (previous
generation does not affect the current generation) and JoaCarpet is not
memoryless (has a counter that remembers how many times random has been
called). JoaCarpet's approach is to start off with the most extreme numbers: 0
and 1. When the counter reaches 1, it resets, and automatically increase the
number of cuts so that the next iteration will loop through 0, 0.5, and 1. One
major issue with this approach is that it requires manual user input to reset
the counter and the counter are shared between all item entity randomlization
events. If you have multiple droppers doing the same thing, some of the
droppers might never hit the edge cases. After leaving JoaCarpet insane
behavior running for hours, you can encounter dropper basically dispensing
items at the same location. This is because the "cuts" value is getting way too
big so the increment step between each item dispense is almost 0.

---

## Cave Ecosystems

Each of the 7 regions has its own unique cave vegetation – on floors and ceilings – so you can instantly recognise where you are, even deep underground.

### Mountains

![Mountain Caves](https://cdn.modrinth.com/data/cached_images/ca94829e4829bbb3711b31796e2c83234cc1e53a.jpeg)

![Arid Caves](https://cdn.modrinth.com/data/cached_images/1bae549b1dddb6db15a41687f2f39a69e5c7b535.jpeg)

### Aquatic

### Snowy

![Snowy Caves](https://cdn.modrinth.com/data/cached_images/055c78b5644ad93db2c5fc2ee021c134c8017d91.jpeg)

### Magical

![Magical Caves](https://cdn.modrinth.com/data/cached_images/6207eea730857fd17678d5513a5460e915bb84ca.jpeg)

---

## Compass – Always Know What to Mine

When holding a **compass** in either hand, an actionbar message appears showing the ores available in your current region. It updates once per second (20 ticks) to reduce performance impact.

![Compass display](https://cdn.modrinth.com/data/cached_images/8fb3bc7b4d2d44eb31b30ce9e3ef28a17217399f_0.webp)

There is also a convenient advancement system that tells you which ores belong to which region. To unlock an entry, simply visit the region and go underground.

---

## New Geodes!

Amethyst geodes are now exclusive to the Magical region. In their place, we’ve added several new geodes with unique contents – and they appear not only in the Overworld, but also in the Nether and the End!

| Geode Type | Where to Find | Special Contents |
|------------|---------------|------------------|
| **Diamond** | Mountain & Snowy biomes | Diamond ore, air‑filled |
| **Emerald** | Calm biomes | Emerald ore, slime blocks, froglight |
| **Lapis** | Aquatic biomes | Lapis ore, prismarine, sea lanterns |
| **Amethyst** | Magical biomes | Amethyst blocks, calcite, buds (tiny & giant variants) |
| **End** | Small End Islands | Raw iron/gold/copper blocks |
| **Nether Quartz** | Nether Wastes | Quartz ore, glowstone |
| **Nether Diamond** | Basalt Deltas | Deepslate diamond ore, filled with lava |

![End Geodes](https://cdn.modrinth.com/data/cached_images/c4a6866407460e0c267d594a8afb5b0f3c768e29.jpeg)

---

## ⚠️ Compatibility & Limitations

### ❌ Incompatibility with some other datapacks

GeoCaves completely overrides **every** vanilla overworld biome, as well as basalt deltas, nether wastes, and small end islands. This means it is **incompatible** with any other datapack that modifies biome JSON files (e.g., global ore rebalancing, world generation overhauls, etc.). Only one such datapack can be active at a time.

### ❌ Modded biomes

GeoCaves **does not affect** biomes added by mods or other datapacks. Those biomes will retain vanilla ore distribution, which breaks the regional balance.

---

## Roadmap

- English translation
- No_Ore_Rebalance version (vanilla ores only, no vegetation)
- NeoForge version with support for popular biome mods
- Backport to Minecraft 1.21.5

title: ItemOfTheDay
description: A lightweight Minecraft Paper server plugin that allows players to exchange a different item each day for a reward.
body:
# ItemOfTheDay

A lightweight Minecraft Paper server plugin that allows players to exchange a different item each day for a reward. Server operators have the ability to set or shuffle the Item of the Day (IOTD), set the reward for the current Item of the Day, and set the default reward, which is reverted back to on date change or when the IOTD is shuffled.

### What's New in v1.0.1

- Added the `/iotd list-claimed` command for server operators to view who's already claimed today's reward
- Minor fixes

### Requirements

Server must have Paper installed. Currently supported versions of Paper include stable builds built for versions `1.21.11` through `26.2` of Minecraft. Use with alpha/beta builds of Paper at your own risk and discretion.

### Commands

- `/iotd info`: available to all players - displays info on the current Item of the Day and corresponding reward.
- `/iotd exchange`: available to all players - if the player has a single instance of the IOTD in their main hand and has not already exchanged today, the IOTD in their hand will be replaced with the current reward.
- `/iotd shuffle`: operator required - randomizes the IOTD and resets the reward back to the specified default reward.
- `/iotd set <item>`: operator required - sets the current IOTD to the specified item WITHOUT changing the reward.
- `/iotd set-reward <reward> <amount>`: operator required - sets the current reward to the specified item and amount.
- `/iotd set-default-reward <default-reward> <amount>`: operator required - sets the default reward (reverted to when IOTD is shuffled) to the specified item and amount.
- `/iotd list-claimed`: operator required - lists all the players who've claimed today's IOTD.
- `/iotd reset-claimed`: operator required - clears the config's list of players (UUIDs) who have already exchanged for the IOTD.

### Config

The plugin creates a config file at `plugins/ItemOfTheDay/config.yml`. All key-value pairs found in the config file can be edited through commands except for the list of `blacklisted-items`, so the only time server owners should have to edit this config file is to add or remove items from the blacklist.

By default, `blacklisted-items` contains all items which are unobtainable in survival mode. Edit the list and restart the server for blacklist changes to take effect.

Support for adding/removing items to and from the blacklist on the fly with commands will be added in a future update.

### Features

- Uses the `ItemType` registry to select items from and validate against, so any custom items added by mods or plugins will be included in IOTD by default.
- Supports command arguments of type `ItemStack` for the reward commands, allowing server operators to create unique custom rewards using the same syntax as the Vanilla `/give` command.
- `DateWatcher`: a lightweight class that keeps track of the current date by checking against a saved `LocalDate` every 1 minute (1200 ticks). Note that this is based on server ticks, so if ticks do not occur when players are offline on your server, the IOTD will be shuffled the first time someone joins on a new date (within a minute).

### Contributing

Contribute at [github.com/timnorthrop/ItemOfTheDay](https://github.com/timnorthrop/ItemOfTheDay).

title: Create: Take a seat, Piglin! - Automated Bartering
description: Create Addon to Automate Piglin bartering with belts and depots
body:
**Automate piglin bartering with Create.**

![Example](https://media.forgecdn.net/attachments/1749/801/ponderwonder-png.png)

## At a glance

*   A seated piglin barters your gold into loot, no clicking required.
*   Reads gold off a Create depot or a moving belt.
*   Same drop table as vanilla bartering. Nothing rebalanced.
*   Slip a gold block under the seat and it watches a wider area.
*   Bonus: you can finally leash a calm piglin, which vanilla won't let you do.
*   A built-in Ponder walks you through the whole thing in-game.
*   Needs Create on NeoForge, Minecraft 1.21.1.

## Why I made this

Bartering pays out well, but doing it is a chore. You toss an ingot, wait for the admire animation, grab the drop, then do it all again. Once your factory is humming it feels silly that you're the slowest part of the line. So I made a mod that handles it for you.

## Setup

1) Sit the piglin on a Create **seat** so it can't wander off.

2) Give it a **name tag** so it won't despawn.

3) Make sure it's an **adult**. Babies won't trade.

4) Put **gold ingots** on a depot or belt right next to it.

Have fun automating the sorting of the loot you get!

## Learn it in-game

No need to leave the game to read this. The mod ships with Create's **Ponder** scenes, so you can watch the whole setup animate in front of you. Hover over a **gold ingot** in your inventory (or in JEI/EMI) and press **W** to open it. Three scenes walk through the basics: the depot bartering loop, the detection range and gold-block boost, and several piglins trading in parallel.

## How it works

*   **Gold on a depot:** the piglin trades it in place and the loot drops into the depot's output.
*   **Gold on a belt:** it waits for the ingot to reach its closest point, stops it, turns to face it, then puts the loot back on the belt to ride on.
*   A trade takes 120 ticks, about six seconds, matching the vanilla admire time.
*   It searches a **3×3×3** cube by default. Park a **block of gold** under the seat and that grows to **7×7×7**, big enough for one piglin to cover a few belts at once.
*   **Leashing:** you can put a lead on any calm piglin. Brutes and angry ones still shrug it off.

Loot comes straight from a bartering loot table, so the odds match trading by hand. Trade time and both ranges live in the config if you want to tweak them.

## Requirements

*   **Create** required, this is an add-on.
*   **NeoForge** for **Minecraft 1.21.1**.

## Modpacks

Feel free to use my mods in your modpack, just don't forget to give proper credit.

## Other Mods by me

I run these mods together:

*   [Empty Hand Keybind - Hold Onto THIS](https://www.curseforge.com/minecraft/mc-mods/hold-onto-this)
*   [PAPA: Portable Aeronautics Physics Assembler](https://www.curseforge.com/minecraft/mc-mods/papa-portable-aeronautics-physics-assembler) - Addon for [Create Aeronautics](https://www.curseforge.com/minecraft/mc-mods/create-aeronautics)
*   [Create Safe Seating](https://www.curseforge.com/minecraft/mc-mods/create-safe-seating) \- Addon for Create

title: Isocraft
description: Isometric view + ARPG-like gameplay to minecraft
body: # Isocraft **Isocraft turns Minecraft into a stylized isometric game** a Project-Zomboid / Diablo / League-of-Legends camera with cursor aim, click-to-move, and a smart reveal system that lifts away whatever is between you and your character so you can *always* see yourself. It's **100% client-side**, works with **Sodium & Iris**, and it's a **toggle** — press one key to drop into iso, press it again to go back to vanilla. Fabric   Minecraft 1.21.11   Client-side   Singleplayer + Multiplayer ## ✨ What makes it special Isocraft isn't a texture pack or a shader — it re-frames the entire game. Press O and the camera pulls back into a cinematic isometric angle, your character starts aiming at your cursor, and the world reshapes itself so nothing ever hides you. ![Isometric View Camping](https://cdn.modrinth.com/data/cached_images/eff5816d9172c2e952b65ab55aa6addc5aa0c5f7.jpeg) ![Elytra Travel](https://cdn.modrinth.com/data/cached_images/b8ffa2c77cf9afb7a7729dd00f8f0ce089990019.jpeg) ## 🏠 The Reveal — *"only my room"* The heart of the mod. Step indoors, underground, or into a structure and the walls, ceilings and floors between the camera and **the room you're standing in** simply lift away — like a dollhouse. Everything else stays put. No X-ray, no floating geometry — just your space, opened up. - **Any shape, any renderer.** Caves, L-shaped rooms, trial chambers, towers — the reveal follows the *actual* space you're in, and it looks identical whether you run vanilla, **Sodium**, or **Iris**. - **See-through outdoors.** Trees, hills and cliffs between the camera and your character turn **transparent in a soft circle** around you, then solidify again as you move — you're never lost behind a hill or a canopy. - **Fog-of-war mood.** Everything outside your space fades toward darkness. Slide the **Exterior Brightness** control from pure black (survival-horror) to a dim fog (dungeon-crawler) to taste. - **It hears the room too.** Sounds coming from outside your space are **muffled** — a zombie two walls over is quiet until you open the door. ![Inside a Room, Dollhouse](https://cdn.modrinth.com/data/cached_images/e65343bd52c4ad82b9b1a8d539d8fe43e01d10bd.jpeg) ## 🎯 Cursor aim & ARPG movement Your character looks and aims exactly where your cursor points — in full 3D, so **bows and projectiles line up with what you're pointing at**, height and all. Movement is screen-relative (push a direction, go that way), just like an isometric action game. - **Click-to-move** *(optional)* — hold to walk where you point, Diablo-style. Toggle it on in settings. - **Ride & steer** — boats and horses steer toward your cursor. - **Swim your way** — Space rises, Shift dives, and you hold depth in between. - **Elytra** — cursor steers your heading, Space climbs, Shift dives. ## 🧱 Bridge Assist — build to the hidden side In an isometric view you can't click the faces that point *away* from the camera — exactly the sides you need to bridge outward. Isocraft fixes that **Bedrock-style**: hold a block, point just past an edge, and a **hologram** of your block appears against the hidden face. Right-click to place it — hold and drag to bridge continuously. - Previews the real orientation (stairs, slabs, logs). - The green marker only appears when the placement will actually work. - Left-click stays safe — you can't accidentally mine the block under your feet. ![Bridge Assist](https://cdn.modrinth.com/data/cached_images/c902f17794ff3c90cd4523081ecb65f7961ea4e7.jpeg) ## ⚔️ Combat & loot juice An ARPG camera deserves ARPG feedback. | Feature | What it does | |---|---| | **Health & hunger orbs** | Pixel-art orb HUD in place of the vanilla bars | | **Floating damage numbers** | Pop off mobs as you hit them | | **Loot beams** | Rarity-tinted pillars of light on dropped items | | **Nameplates** | Floating health bars + names over mobs | | **Threat silhouettes** | Monsters hidden behind walls glow so they can't ambush you blind | | **Damage-direction ping** | A red tick flashes toward off-screen hits | | **Player light halo** | Keeps a readable circle of light around you at night / in caves | | **Context cursor** | The cursor tells you what a click will do — walk, mine, use, attack, or build | ![Features](https://cdn.modrinth.com/data/cached_images/1121fddee0d1c86dcd25c3ea5b615009cb4689c0.jpeg) ## 🛋️ Quality of life - **Bubble menus** — chests, furnaces and crafting UIs float *over the block* in the world instead of covering the screen. - **In-game settings** with **live preview** — drag a slider and watch the world react, no reloads. Press the settings key any time. - **Three one-click presets** — **Survivor** (hard black, tense), **Dungeon** (dim fog), **Cozy** (bright and warm). - **Gentle onboarding** — tiny one-time hint cards teach each system the first time it's relevant, then never again. - **Diorama Shot** — press F6 for a clean, HUD-free screenshot of your build. (That's how you make the pictures on this very page.) ![Bubble Menus and Settings](https://cdn.modrinth.com/data/cached_images/f9ad30275d9fa493b3ffc239f083abe57ee67787.jpeg) ## 🎛️ Controls | Action | Key | |---|---| | Toggle isometric view | O | | Zoom | Mouse wheel | | Rotate camera | , / . | | Pitch up / down | Page Up / Page Down | | Settings | *(bindable)* | | Bow aim arc on/off | *(bindable)* | | Diorama screenshot | F6 | *Everything is rebindable in Options → Controls, and every feature can be toggled in the Isocraft settings screen.* ## 🧩 Compatibility - ✅ **Client-side only** — install it yourself, play on any server (vanilla or modded), nobody else needs it. - ✅ **Sodium** & **Iris** supported — the reveal matches the vanilla look on both. - ✅ Works alongside most content and QoL mods. - ⚠️ **Distant Horizons / Voxy** — not officially supported yet. - ⚠️ Requires **Fabric API**. ## 📦 Install 1. Install **Fabric Loader** for Minecraft **1.21.11**. 2. Drop **Fabric API** and **Isocraft** into your `mods` folder. 3. Launch, load a world, and press O. *(Sodium and Iris are optional — Isocraft detects them and adapts automatically.)* ## ❓ FAQ **Does it work in multiplayer?** Yes. It's purely visual/local — the server never knows. **Do I have to play in iso the whole time?** No. It's a toggle. Press O to switch views whenever you like. **Does it change gameplay or give an advantage?** No stats, no cheats — it's a camera and a UI. The reveal only shows the room you're already in; it doesn't X-ray through the world. **Known rough edges (being honest):** - A couple of block types (chests, beds, signs) show only an outline instead of a full hologram in Bridge Assist — they still place fine. - The settings screen gets a little cramped at very high GUI scales on small monitors.

body:
This mod replaces the default item and experience pickup sounds with the emerald pickup sound from Minecraft Dungeons.

<iframe width="560" height="315" src="https://www.youtube-nocookie.com/embed/Q8e_nNRFBnU" title="YouTube video player" frameborder="0" allow="accelerometer; autoplay; clipboard-write; encrypted-media; gyroscope; picture-in-picture; web-share" allowfullscreen></iframe>

Unlike a standard resource pack, **this mod processes audio dynamically** based on how quickly items are collected. When multiple items are picked up at once, **the sounds are queued sequentially rather than playing simultaneously**. The audio pitch increases as the collection combo continues, creating an accelerated speed effect. Once the combo ends, a heavy "Burst Finale" sound effect plays. This sound signals that the combo window has reset.

**The mod features two detection modes:**

* Broad (Default): Intercepts the pickup sound effect itself. This replaces the audio for all actions using that sound, including collecting arrows or tridents. While less immersive, it offers maximum compatibility with external mods, such as those adding item magnets.
  
* Strict: Functions exclusively when the player collects experience or items. Actions like picking up arrows or tridents retain their default sounds. This mode is also stack-size aware, meaning collecting a large item stack automatically initiates a combo proportional to the stack size.

**This mod is highly configurable.**

title: Rubric
description: Multi-loader Minecraft mod configuration library.
body:
# Rubric

A multi-loader Minecraft mod configuration library.

## Philosophy

Rubric does what YetAnotherConfigLib ([YACL](https://modrinth.com/mod/yacl)) originally set out to do: be a *configuration library* — and nothing more. It defines your config, loads and saves it, validates and migrates it, and syncs it between server and client. It does not draw the settings screen itself.

Where YACL grew into a full configuration-plus-GUI framework, Rubric stops at the library layer and leaves the frontend to whichever config-screen library the user already has
installed. Today that means [YACL](https://modrinth.com/mod/yacl) and [Cloth Config](https://modrinth.com/mod/cloth-config), with more frontends possible via the `ScreenProvider` SPI. If neither is installed, Rubric still loads and edits your config on
disk — the in-game screen falls back to a placeholder that points the user at the config file.

## Scope

- Loader-agnostic core, with a Fabric integration module (NeoForge planned).
- Annotation-driven or programmatic config definition.
- Correct-and-log validation, versioned migrations, and an event bus for change notifications.
- Server-authoritative sync with per-entry scope control.
- Pluggable format adapters (TOML, JSON, JSON5) and IO backends.

## Status

Early. APIs may still shift.

## License

MIT.

title: World Switcher
description: Server-side Multiverse-style world manager: switch worlds with /ws, import and manage world saves with /wsc, per-player per-world inventories. Vanilla clients can join - no client install needed.
body:
# World Switcher
Run **multiple worlds on one server** and let players switch between them with a single command - Multiverse-style, but for NeoForge.
**100% server-side**: no client installation needed. Vanilla 1.21.1 clients can join without the mod.
## Features
- **/ws <world>** - switch worlds instantly, no server restart. Bare /ws lists all worlds (clickable).
- **/wsc** - full world management for operators: create <name> [seed], import <folder> [as <name>], rename, load, unload, tp <player> <world>, info, delete (with confirmation).
- **Per-player, per-world inventories** (optional, on by default): inventory, ender chest, XP, health, hunger, effects and last position are kept separately for every world. The vanilla dimensions (overworld/nether/end) count as one group.
- **World import done right**: copies only the overworld data, reads seed & spawn from the source level.dat, so terrain keeps generating seamlessly beyond the imported border. Old worlds (1.18+) are upgraded on the fly.
- **Persistent**: registered worlds are re-loaded automatically at server start.
- **Safe renaming**: display names are decoupled from the internal world id - inventories, bed spawns and world folders survive renames.

## Edge cases handled
- Nether portals inside the default world group don't touch your inventory.
- Portals that cross world groups swap the player state like /ws would (configurable).
- Dying in a world without a bed respawns you in the default world with your default state - your items stay at the death spot in the other world.
- If a world is deleted while you're offline in it, you're safely reconciled into the overworld on login.

## Configuration
See world/serverconfig/worldswitcher-server.toml: separateInventories (default true), wsPermissionLevel (0 = everyone may use /ws), worldsFolder (import folder, default worlds), autoLoadOnStartup, restoreLastPosition, handlePortalGroupChanges.
## Notes
- Time, weather and gamerules are shared across all worlds (like the vanilla nether/end).
- Map mods (BlueMap etc.) will see the extra dimensions and may need per-dimension config.

title: Drop Randomizer
description: Makes every item drop caused by a player random, configurable.
body:
# Drop Randomizer

A Paper plugin that replaces every block and mob drop with a random item from the full item pool. Drop amounts are preserved — only the item type changes.

**Compatible with Paper 1.20.6+ and 26.1+.**

## Overview

- **Block breaks** (player-initiated): drop is replaced with a random item.
- **Cascade breaks** (sugar cane, bamboo, kelp): each block in the cascade is individually randomized.
- **Mob kills**: each drop is replaced with a random item.
- Fishing, loot chests, and other loot table sources are unaffected.

## Commands

| Command | Permission | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `/randomizer reload` | `randomizer.admin` (default: op) | Reloads config and rebuilds the item pool. |

## Configuration

`plugins/Randomizer/config.yml`:

```yaml
keep-vanilla:
  items: []
  groups: []

exclude-from-pool:
  items: []
  groups:
    - ADMIN_BLOCKS
```

### `keep-vanilla`

Blocks listed here drop their normal vanilla items instead of a random one.

```yaml
keep-vanilla:
  items:
    - DIRT
    - STONE
  groups:
    - ORES
```

### `exclude-from-pool`

Items listed here are removed from the random draw and can never appear as a drop result.

```yaml
exclude-from-pool:
  items:
    - BEDROCK
  groups:
    - ADMIN_BLOCKS
    - SPAWN_EGGS
```

## Groups

Pre-defined groups usable in both `keep-vanilla` and `exclude-from-pool`:

| Group | Contents |
|---|---|
| `WOOL` | All 16 wool colors |
| `CONCRETE` | All 16 concrete colors |
| `CONCRETE_POWDER` | All 16 concrete powder colors |
